title: Orchestrate groupable shell-step runbooks with dry-run and RBAC guardrails
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description:
Problem: Support engineers and on-call SREs frequently run multi-step shell procedures that span systems (database failovers, cache evictions, model node drains). Current runbooks live as ad-hoc markdowns and long bash scripts. We lack: (1) composable grouping of steps, (2) dry-run validation, (3) per-step RBAC & approval gates, (4) audit-friendly structured outputs for Console ingestion. This increases toil and the chance of human error during incidents.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight orchestration layer around existing runbook steps ("shell-step groups") that: (a) allows creating named groups of ordered steps with templated inputs, (b) performs a validation/dry-run mode that checks env/permissions and prints a simulated execution plan, (c) enforces RBAC at group and step granularity with optional human approval steps, (d) emits structured audit events to the existing observability pipeline for Console and incident postmortems, and (e) integrates with Ops Assistant and the Playbook Scheduler to allow scheduled/parametrized runs.

Implementation notes: We'll add a service-level controller that consumes YAML runbook-group manifests stored in a secure internal repo. Each step is a small JSON/YAML object: {"id","type":"shell|k8s|api","cmd","timeout","retry_policy","sensitive":bool}. The orchestrator will execute steps in a sandboxed runner w/namespace separation and per-run temporary creds (short-lived tokens). A dry-run will validate templates, confirm secrets/creds are resolvable, and produce an execution graph without mutating state. RBAC will be wired into our existing IAM — groups map to permission roles; approval steps surface as ephemeral OIDC prompts integrated with SSO. Audit events will be posted to the same event sink used by Console traces (trace_id, step_id, actor, timestamp, outcome).

Why now: Reduces incident MTTR and human risk, makes runbooks auditable for SOC/compliance, and unlocks scheduled playbook automation for routine maintenance tasks.

Non-goals: We are not building a full workflow DSL or replacing full-scale orchestration engines (e.g., Airflow). This is targeted at operational runbooks for support and SRE flows.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Create at least three runbook-group manifests (db-safe-eviction, node-drain, cache-rollover) with templated inputs and confirm dry-run prints a valid execution plan.
2) Execute a non-destructive group in staged env (staging cluster) and assert all step logs are captured and emitted to the audit sink with trace_id.
3) Verify RBAC-enforced denial: a user without 'runbook:execute' role must be blocked from executing the group and must be able to request/receive an approval for a single-step elevation.
4) Integration: a scheduled job can successfully enqueue and run a runbook-group via the Playbook Scheduler and shows cost/latency traces in Console.
5) Security review completed and SRE runbook owners sign off on step templates for sensitive operations.
